Consumer GPUs and non-confidential hardware serve non-sensitive open-lane work. Operators may see open-lane prompts. Public-model batch inference, embeddings, evaluations and image generation are examples of work that can fit that lane when the inputs are suitable.

Illustrative flow: a GPU provider has verified USDG earnings and wants to choose a payout destination. Selling a separate earnings token is not part of the proposed flow. The provider instead compares a direct USDG wallet claim, a canonical Stock Token claim and a virtual card claim, subject to route conditions.

The claim service builds the selected route against the provider’s cumulative Merkle entitlement. The stock route checks the canonical registry and shows price impact before signing. The card route consumes entitlement on-chain before issuance, tracks the request by claim ID and is designed to refund USDG after issuance failure. A split claim can combine routes.

The design outcome is three intended payout routes sharing a single claimed balance. Card regions and program terms, as well as Stock Token eligibility and liquidity, shape availability. This is an illustrative specification flow, not a record of issued cards, completed customer payouts or financial returns.

p: One path from GPU to receipt

Illustrative flow: a GPU provider wants to supply suitable compute and understand how a completed AI job becomes a work record. The provider needs a benchmarked GPU, a node identity and a clear distinction between confidential hardware and the open lane. Available hardware does not itself guarantee demand or earnings.

The provider installs the Docker node agent. It benchmarks GPU capability, creates a node key and registers through a passkey smart account. The scheduler matches suitable jobs by lane, VRAM fit, latency, stake and reputation. Completed jobs produce signed receipts; verified work accrues in USDG and enters the next cumulative receipt epoch.

The intended outcome is one view from node registration through job verification and hourly receipt roots. There are two compute lanes in the design and USDG is the unit of earnings. This is a specification walkthrough, with no live node count, utilization promise or projected income.
